trust_decision.summary: The configserver trusts any request that (a) carries an Origin accepted by its CORS middleware and (b) names the app UUID under which the local project is stored; both decisions are made in-process with no credential - at the pinned commit (a) is the allow-everything cors.Default() and (b) is the publicly known constant 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, so any web page can read config, secrets and container logs and write config/secrets.

landing_point.why: The advisory is about cross-origin access to the local configserver; the only cross-origin control in that process is the CORS middleware instance passed to graph.SetupRouter, which at the pinned commit is the permissive cors.Default() from the vendored rs/cors gin wrapper.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The shared oapi CORS middleware lives in internal/lib/oapi and exists for the cloud auth/storage services; the configserver is a hidden CLI dev tool with its own third-party CORS wrapper (rs/cors), so a solver can argue the shared middleware is somebody else's surface and fix only cli/cmd/configserver. For the logs route the argument is stronger: cli/cmd/configserver/logsapi/router.go already ships its own origin allow-list, so 'that route is already protected'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate behaviours sit next to the sinks. (1) A dashboard edit of one secret must preserve every other secret on disk: once GetApps returns redacted placeholders, UpdateSecrets has to merge with the on-disk .secrets (placeholder = untouched, real value = write through, name absent from the payload = delete) instead of writing the payload through, and the placeholder must be >= 64 chars so resolved-config validation (HS512 minimum length) still passes on unrelated updates. (2) The dashboard origin is per-project (nhost dev uses a configurable subdomain, http or https, optional port), so a hard-coded single AllowedOrigins entry silently breaks every dashboard except the default `local` one.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: cli/cmd/configserver/local.go:164-180 (secrets merge) and cli/cmd/configserver/configserver.go:170 (per-project dashboard origin)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebSocket subscription /v1/logs/graphql (same gin engine, container-log sink that the code itself says routinely contains secrets) is gated only by checkWebSocketOrigin, whose policy is looser than the fix's: it accepts any multi-label *.dashboard.local.nhost.run and any http://localhost:PORT / http://127.0.0.1:PORT origin, all of which the new dashboardOriginRe rejects; the fix does not unify the two.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The logs API already had its own origin check from an earlier hardening pass (with a whitebox test at cli/cmd/configserver/logsapi/router_test.go:8-40), and logs are not 'configuration and secrets', so the route reads as already-protected and out of this advisory's scope.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second origin predicate for the HTTP logs endpoints (POST /v1/logs/graphql) written by a maintainer who trusts checkWebSocketOrigin to cover the whole logs group.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already contains a hand-rolled origin allow-list and a whitebox test of it, so a maintainer adding an HTTP mirror of the logs query would naturally copy that predicate rather than reuse the CORS middleware.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A redaction/merge sibling in UpdateRunServiceConfig: run-service configs also carry env values and are serialized to disk from the same GraphQL surface.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the only other write path in the plugin, it sits directly under UpdateSecrets, and it marshals the same kind of model objects; a maintainer redacting secrets would plausibly extend the same placeholder convention here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third container env block (console/mailhog or a new local UI) that needs the per-project app id threaded through, next to the dashboard block.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The compose generator already has one block per local UI service and the fix had to touch two of them (dashboard, dashboardCloud); adding another is the standard pattern in this file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A caller of the shared oapi CORS middleware that sets AllowedOrigins to an origin list built from a user-supplied flag, next to auth's wildcard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every service builds CORSOptions this way; a solver who changes the middleware signature or semantics must chase them, and the storage config already takes origins from a CLI flag.
